As of 11:36 AM ET, the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) is up 1.86% to 24,016, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) has gained 1.38% to 7,282, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) is trading 1.15% higher to 50,760 as technology stocks rebound from recent correction territory.

Gold prices have jumped 1.66% to $3,626.60, while the 10-Year Treasury yield is at 4.96% (-0.07%). All sectors gained, with energy and consumer cyclical stocks outpacing healthcare and consumer defensive sectors.

Today's biggest moves

Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) and Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) jumped 12.74% and 5.96%, respectively, as investors returned to artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. Amazon.com (NASDAQ:AMZN) has climbed 3.81% on strong Black Friday demand. Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) also edged higher as investors digested early Black Friday data, which could indicate the health of consumer spending as we head into the end of the year. Vertex Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ:VRTX) fell after the FDA delayed a decision on a key kidney drug.

What this means for investors

Markets snapped back in today's shortened trading session, as tech stocks bounced and Black Friday spending boosted retailers. Revised data released today showed that Q3 GDP increased by 4.3%, underscoring economic resilience. This, along with initial positive insights into holiday outlays, seems to show spending remains relatively robust.

Major indexes look set to finish the week in the green, and investors are watching to see if this recovery will hold. For investors looking for stock bargains, the important thing is to focus on quality companies with solid fundamentals that you plan to hold for the long term. title: Is Walmart Stock Priced Like 1999 Again?
detail:
Is Walmart Stock Priced Like 1999 Again?
Trefis Team
Fri, November 27, 2026 at 7:42 AM PST 4 min read
WMT
AAPL
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: How Much Of Big Tech's AI Spending Reaches Nvidia?

Walmart's stock rose 26% this fall. That added $215 billion to its value, the most among the fall's 10 biggest percentage gainers. Only Apple added more. But investors now pay $50 for each $1 of Walmart's yearly profit. In December 1999 it cost 58 times profit. The stock then took 12 years to get back to its 1999 price.

Why Do Shoppers Pick Walmart?

Speed, at low prices. Walmart says it can now reach 96% of U.S. homes in under three hours. It can reach 60% in under 30 minutes. More than 80% of its U.S. online orders are filled from a nearby store. Deliveries from stores rose more than 40% last quarter. U.S. online sales grew 23%. Walmart says its grocery share gains were among the highest in three years.

Why Did Investors Pay Up?

Ads and outside sellers grow faster than groceries. Brands pay to be seen on Walmart's app and on its Vizio TVs. Its U.S. advertising grew 37%. Sales by outside sellers on its website grew nearly 50%. Walmart says its online business, before ad income, is now close to breaking even.

So profit grows faster than sales. Adjusted operating income, the profit from running the business, rose 5.5%. Sales rose 4.4%. Both figures leave out currency swings.

How Much Is In The Price?

A lot. At Wednesday's close of about $132, Walmart costs 50 times its profit per share over the four quarters through October. On Aug 31 it cost 38 times, and a year ago 37. Its 10-year norm is 33. The fall's 26% rise won back a summer slide. The stock was $132 on April 30, already at 48 times profit. It then fell to $105 by Aug 31.

Walmart's price is far above its 10-year norm. If you are waiting for that price, your cash does not have to sit idle. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

What Happened The Last Time?

Profit grew. The stock didn't. On Dec 27, 1999, Walmart closed at $23.15, adjusted for later splits. That was about 58 times that year's profit of 40 cents a share. Over the next 12 years, profit per share nearly quadrupled, to $1.51. That is growth of about 12% a year. Yet the stock first closed above its 1999 high only on June 29, 2012.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Investors are increasingly turning to defensive stocks as the S&P 500 (SPY) struggles with mounting volatility, signaling a notable shift in market sentiment that could benefit household names such as Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT), Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO) and Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG).

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Sign with MO.

Is SPY fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The consumer staples sector (XLP) has gained 4.1% over the past month, outperforming all 10 other S&P 500 sectors, while the broader benchmark has shed 6.1%, according to Seeking Alpha.

The divergence is particularly striking given the weakness in technology stocks.

The information technology sector (XLK) has plunged 15.2% over the same period, making it the market's worst-performing sector, followed by energy (XLE), which has dropped 12.7%.

For much of the recent bull market, investors have been willing to pay hefty premiums for technology companies promising explosive earnings growth.

However, businesses selling everyday necessities are becoming increasingly attractive as investors seek more predictable earnings and cash flows.

After all, Americans may postpone purchasing a new smartphone or expensive electronics when economic uncertainty increases, but they still need groceries, toothpaste and household cleaning products.

Interestingly, financial stocks have outperformed the broader market across all four periods examined by Seeking Alpha, suggesting that opportunities extend beyond traditionally defensive businesses.

Meanwhile, despite its recent selloff, the energy sector remains up 37.5% over the past year, substantially ahead of the S&P 500's 6.2% gain.

Investors Takeaway

The latest rotation raises an important question for investors heading into 2027: Is Wall Street temporarily seeking shelter or moving away from expensive growth stocks more sustainably?

Investors should closely monitor technology earnings revisions, consumer staples valuations and upcoming Federal Reserve decisions.

However, defensive stocks are not necessarily cheap. Recent market analysis indicates that consumer staples are trading above 24 times earnings, potentially limiting further upside.

Moreover, a recovery in technology earnings expectations could quickly reverse the current rotation.

The biggest takeaway is that market leadership is changing, exposing the risks of portfolios heavily concentrated in technology stocks.
